failure_summary: Both runs fail, on different axes, and both are model-side against a clean render: run 0 emitted an unoffered [term:central] slug although render_decision.zones.terms is [] and the assembled prompt says verbatim 'Do NOT tag any phrase as a named term anywhere in your `mechanism` — there is no slug offered' (G7b_offered fail), and also inverted the render's own L7 swindle frame ('Column 2 ... makes it easier for your opponent to ... keep the practical swindle going', where lostResource.kind=conditional_swindle is the PLAYER's resource that column 2 gives up — L7 text: 'The move you played gives that up and lets your opponent finish faster'); run 1 never names column 4 in prose (A6 fail, mechanical), wrapping [zone:better-col] around 'the more central column' instead, although the prompt's Decision block states 'Better move: column 4 (lands at c4r2)'. MODEL REGIME CAVEAT: these rows are gpt-5.4-mini, the model production ships, so this is a production-fidelity run and prompt_confusion here cannot be separated from model capability — the render layer itself is clean on every model-independent check (G2-G6 pass on both runs, annotationRepairs empty, guardDiagnostics.failures empty).
notes: n_runs=2 for this run (not 5), so no axis was sub-sampled — A3/A4/G2/G4/G5 were graded on both runs and no per_run value is null. Board: movestring '3' (one opponent disc at c4r1), player=2, boardState='opening', case=lose_to_faster_lose, playedCol=1 (display col 2), bestCol=3 (display col 4). A5b applies (player 2 + opening) and BOTH runs pass it: each frames column 4 positively as the tougher/most stubborn defense keeping future four-in-a-row lines alive, with no 'you are losing' and no defeatist closing clause. A4 run 0 fail: 'Column 2 gives up that central hold, so it is easier for your opponent to steer the game and keep the practical swindle going' — false; the conditional swindle (lostResource, pliesToEnd 35 vs opponentPunishment 37) is the blunderer's own resource and is exactly what column 2 surrenders; no charitable parse makes the played move keep it alive. G1 run 0 fail: same sentence contradicts the rendered L7 frame it was built from. G7 run 0 fail via the pre-computed G7b_offered ('unoffered term slug(s) central'); the offered set in render_decision.zones is exactly {better-col->col4, played-col->col2} with terms: [] and requiredSet: []. G7 run 1 pass: both emitted handles are offered, each wraps a phrase matching its role ('the more central column'->better-col, 'the edge-leaning column you chose'->played-col), nothing over-wrapped, annotationRepairs []. A6 run 0 pass / run 1 fail copied verbatim from fv_suff_answers_boards_2026-08-06T16-04-29Z_served_mechanical.json. G5 verified board-true: projectedDeep tactics (immediate c6r3 opp, major c6r4 you, c6r5 opp, c6r6 you) match ./visualize_board.sh on lostResource.finalMovestring '33023202260000211111132633444444666655' exactly, and projectedDeepOpp 'major at c1r6 (you)' matches ./visualize_board.sh on render_decision.finalMovestring '311313113034444434152222226666555556600' exactly. G4: neither mechanism names any cell, so nothing to verify against finalMovestring; key_cells are the col4/col2 zone expansions (condition D display-overlay exception). G3: the two shown:false boards (afterBest/afterPlayed, 'tag-set identical to the decision board') were not needed by either answer. G6: patternOnAfterBestBoard is null and L7 is the correct sign-route link for lose_to_faster_lose. A7 passes on both runs: cause (centrality -> more four-in-a-row lines) not outcome, both referents locatable via emitted col4/col2 zones that survived the guard, not a fork (A7c N/A), and a named idea anchored to the two specific columns at issue. CAVEAT on Step 0b: the reconstructed prompt is anachronistic for this 2026-08-06 run — current renderReasonModel.mjs emits 6 zone aliases and a 3-handle required set (you-key-square/opp-key-square/you-key-line), while this row's recorded render_decision has 2 aliases and requiredSet []; per Step 0 I used render_decision as ground truth for the offered set, and the model's actual output (only better-col/played-col used, no required-handle omissions charged) is consistent with that.
